reason: Umbrella for changing Metaform code. Four narrow project skills (ticket work, module verbs/settings, web page and browser tests, agent body embodiment) are all development work on the same repo with the same test and scope discipline. Each sibling's rules are carried whole into references/ and pointed at from a short labeled body. Re-staged with a description inside the 60-char index budget; the first attempt was rejected on description length.

Worker agents on tickets were refused op=add and need the note-based handoff; orchestrator instruction routes spec drafts to artifacts/specs-draft/; stale memory observations about a replaced design were left behind and had to be removed.

The dispatch_agent_options rewrite showed that one shared list setting drops entries on save; a settings-meaning change needed a migration and restart note; CLI completion needed discovery to run in the completer path.
The elicitation rule was missed because the description does not name agent questions, AskUserQuestion or dispatch. Widen the trigger so the skill loads for that work.

Rich's rule, 2026-10-14: workers must not put questions to the person. Elicitation had been left as the one route for agent questions to reach him after `map ask` was removed. The gate, the decide answer and the test setup are not in the skill, so the next session would restore the old behaviour.

A browser test started a system agent's runner and never stopped it. The run output then listed a leftover metaform dispatch process. Tests that start runners need an explicit stop, which the skill does not mention.
Mid-run, the ticket's task was replaced and the notice said not to restore the old question buttons. The agent had to re-read the ticket to get the new task. The skill has no rule for this.
Roundtable spend/rounds work hit both pitfalls: settings.number is int-only, and an agent could otherwise open a table past a person-only limit.
A throwaway check file failed collection until it carried a kind marker; the no-new-test-files rule in the person's CLAUDE.md should be stated next to it.
Strict pyright rejected a .get on an Any-typed reply; the cast-first fix passed and is the repeatable pattern.

Three lessons from the Space-to-talk ticket: (1) the browser check recipe for the web GUI (private server on a temp home, fake mic, CSP blocks string predicates, stubbed voice endpoints) was rediscovered by trial and error and is not in the skill; (2) a key that starts a mode must not leave focus in a text box, or the next press types; (3) the shared tree had someone else's uncommitted edits in keys.js, so the agent edited one line and did not commit. Patched into the existing web and tickets sections rather than a new skill. Description shortened to fit the index budget.

Ticket 67c956b9 found three browser-check pitfalls not in the reference: a Promise predicate in wait_for_function returns at once, pictures from a non-person camera show mirrored signs unless the labels are turned for that render, and the mascot body can be a bare Object3D with frames paused. Folded into the existing web browser-check reference and pointed to from the Web page section.

The VIEW-051 episode hit three repeatable web-page pitfalls: a depth filter applied in only one builder, a settings read that raced the async save (assert '3' == 'all'), and a 'node not found' console error that failed the problems check. None is in the skill yet.

Dispatch thread line numbering moved to a shared helper with a cursor gotcha and a silent-failure mode; the existing skill has no dispatch section and future edits to runner/serve would repeat the same mistakes.
The episode ran into a concurrent session editing the same test and runner files; the rule to re-read and to avoid file swaps is not in the skill yet.
Episode diagnosed a 'shared session' report from short ids that were only prefix-equal; the lesson is a durable debugging rule for dispatch and roundtable sessions.
Three test-authoring defects hit in one run (B023 loop capture, walrus-in-comprehension SyntaxError, a test inserted mid-function) each cost a rerun; the fixes belong with the existing test rules.

A new home-permission rule (0700 home, 0600 files via sqlite.private and web.write_run, make_private at startup) and a test pitfall (0755 loosening keeps owner x) came out of H13 work; no existing section covers file modes.
Routing: the new home-permission section must be reachable from the words a user types for that class of task, which the current description does not name.

In a shared tree, the agent saw a pyright error in cli.py and a ruff overflow on another session's import line; the rule for which errors are yours was implicit and the agent edited another session's line once.
op=plan silently ignored the numbered plan passed in said; the agent had to re-record the plan inside op=step. Future ticket workers should not lose their plan text.

The browser tests were silently excluded from every run including CI (finding H20). The working command, the -m override and the workflow validation method were all discovered this episode and are needed by anyone touching the page or CI.

The CI path filter for browser tests covers web, mcp, scripts, conftest and build files only. Chassis changes that feed the page's server reads are unguarded. Agents editing those paths need to know the gap rather than assume CI covers the page.

Rich's rule, stated this episode, is that code is the reference over specs; the skill only forbade editing spec records and did not forbid the reverse (changing code to match a spec). Stops a future session from rolling back features to satisfy a stale record.
The episode's ticket board showed 5 of 8 steps because several steps were recorded in one note; per-step notes keep the board honest.
Five hosting settings were made person_only this episode; the skill described the limit behaviour but not that the MCP schema must omit such settings and the refusal helper must cover them.
A concrete, reproducible test-ordering crash hit this episode; the fix is a one-line ordering rule that a future test writer would otherwise rediscover.
Cross-link: every new page write must be classed in the one route table, which this skill's web section did not mention.

Refactor sent source code to OpenRouter with no consent switch (review C2). The fix makes the person-only jev setting the gate for every outbound Jev request, through metaform.jev, and declares outbound verbs honestly. No existing section states the consent rule, so it goes in as a new section ahead of the agent-body section.

Testing the refactor intake follow-on took several failed runs before the stub worked: intake finish reloads modules, so a stub on an old module object misses the code that runs, and a patched subprocess.Popen breaks import mcp. The shared client's 429 retry also changed which HTTP status a test may use. Recorded once in memory; belongs in the test rules where the next agent will look.

Three page defects in one ticket shared two patterns the skill does not yet name: currentTarget read after an await, and a read path that writes a setting. The mascot open act also dead-ended silently via the overlay opener. Patch into the web page section where these rules belong.

The existing rule forbids copying aside in general, but the ticket proved the fail-without-fix check safely by copying the whole tree to /tmp and reversing only its own hunks; the shared tree was never touched. Reconciling the rule so the next session uses the safe form rather than skipping the proof.

Settings rules from this episode (H1, H3, H4, H5 on code.manager.configuration#5) were implemented in settings.py and the surfaces, but the skill's settings section does not yet tell the next author to declare per_call/risky or to write at own scope. Without it the same defects get reintroduced one surface at a time.

The agent-prompts browser test had failed on HEAD for a long time because it never opened the dispatch page; the fix is a navigation rule the next browser test for any module setting will need. The confirm rule is the page half of the risky-choice rule.
A lint finding on a line the agent had just written blocked the final checks until fixed; a one-line rule prevents the rework on the next test that splits a long assert message.

Ticket code.server.tool#5 found five verbs with wrong annotations (refactor associate read, intake finish, dispatch signals, raise, run) that the existing principle already forbade; the reach test now catches them, and effect changes ripple into consumers that filter by effect.

In the H17 change the agent updated the module READMEs and CHANGELOG but had to find the MCP reference table rows separately; the table is generated from the server, so a declaration change that skips it leaves the doc wrong. Also records that modules without a CHANGELOG get none.

During a module rename the start hook, once wired, migrated the real ~/.metaform in another live process before the agent had finished testing it; the scratch-home check and the marker-in-test-home gotcha were only discovered after that.
The rename of refactor to source_placement touched all these surfaces; the agent had to discover each one, and the memories citing old paths had to be replaced after the fact.
Removing the roundtable module surfaced a repeatable procedure (orphan imports, load-order chain, 403-vs-404 route check, untracked deletes, running servers) that no existing section covers.
The existing rule was broken again in the same way: two range notes, and the board read 4 of 9. The rule needs the explicit range case.
The private-server check ran with the session's METAFORM_* variables cleared, then confirmed the port freed after stop. That cleanup step is not written anywhere in the skill.

The seat support was deleted from this repo, so the line describing a seat's decline in Metaform is stale. Stated as a superseded fact, not deleted outright, because the roundtable server still exists.
The roundtable seats' read-only tool set no longer exists in Metaform: the seat code was deleted in the same change, so the example names a consumer that is gone.
That sentence describes the roundtable table's seat status, which left Metaform with the seat code on 2026-10-14. The rule about comparing whole session ids stands without it.
Recording memory for work in a sibling repo failed on citation paths; the rule is the project-folder boundary of the memory tool, which this skill covers for Metaform memory work.

The agent-view fix kept the mode across A cycling through none, and the saved-camera guard prevented a midway return; both are rules for any page mode that tweens the camera, and the existing web section governs that work.
make_private recorded home_private while a symlinked home stayed 0755; the docs now describe the link resolution and the post-check gate that the fix added.

Found while verifying the make_private fix: a fresh 0700 home still gets 0755 folders from add project and other mkdirs. The skill lists only the file gap, so a future session would miss the folder gap.
A test used monkeypatch.setenv to point the CLI at a link; the run fixture overrode it, so the test failed even with the fix in place. The gotcha belongs with the test rules.
The dispatch migration marker was tightened from 0644 to 0600 with the same os.open pattern; the skill should name it so the next writer copies the pattern.

Recurring defect: a start hook that moves project-folder files ran from a scratch copy of the real home and moved the person's live runs. The existing rule only said to test against a scratch home, not that copies carry real project paths. Also records the one-marker-per-step trap hit when the run move was added under an already-written marker.
The rename instruction still sends run folders to a project-folder .metaform path, which the module no longer uses; runs now live under the home, and a rename must move them there.

On 2026-10-14 map add-base, activate and collapse gained caution=BASE_SWITCH. The CLI enforces caution too, so four existing test calls broke until --confirm was added; the doc and README changes were needed alongside. The skill covered effect/open_world rows but not caution, and the CLI enforcement was discovered by grep only.
The guard test passed green while blind to most write verbs; the only way it was found was a deliberate mutation. The skill's test section should require that proof for any source-walking guard.

The page and server split free-text list settings at every comma, contradicting the stated rule that lists are stored member by member. Ticket 9df95e33 fixed the page (one item per line textarea) and the server (400 on a string for a list); the skill should state the implemented behaviour and the remaining CLI/fallback comma path.

The settings window opens on the Modules page, so browser tests that touch chassis rows time out at their first line. The existing guidance only covered module rows and was incomplete. The stale header comment also shows a change to a control needs its doc comments checked.

The marker-ticket change would have started paid agents on eleven pre-existing markers the moment it loaded live. The agent noticed this only at the end, in the final report. A rule to count and disclose live effects before landing prevents that next time.

The rule says spec text never goes into specifications/, but the owner approved the MAP-046 rule and the agent had to write the amendment into specifications/01-map.md and 09-viewer.md. The skill needs the approved-text path stated, so the two rules stop contradicting each other.

Ticket code.interface.graphical#43 showed that `web open ticket id=<id>` could not open a real ticket: the request token overwrote the noun named `id`, and `open` was missing from MASCOT_ASKS so the verb never waited for the page's answer. The existing bullet names openFor but not these two traps, which a future mascot act would hit again.
An Edit succeeded with a staleRecovered note and the agent had to verify its hunks survived concurrent writes from another session; the rule should say to check after the last edit.
Every browser test run in the episode was prefixed with the unset; the rule currently covers only the private server, so a test run from an agent shell is left unprotected.

Two gaps hit this episode: the metaform MCP server failed to connect (No module named 'yaml'), and memory observations had to be corrected through the CLI, whose argument shapes are not written down. Added the fallback rule (say so, use the CLI, name the failure in the ticket) and the exact delete/add shapes.
A whole-tree pytest run failed at collection on a basename collision between two test files; the rule prevents a silent full-suite break and tells the agent to leave another session's file alone.

On 2026-10-14 the elevenlabs module's model choices called ElevenLabs on every tools/list; a 3 s hold made each list take 3.1-3.4 s. The fix moved the choices to a project table and recorded the place limit. The rule belongs with module settings.

The W2I-F2 ticket edited MCP-041's and MCP-043's Built notes and the Acceptance gap was left for Rich; the existing rule forbids spec edits from tickets, so the rule needs to name Built lines explicitly.

Two test-harness gotchas cost the W2I-F2 episode several probe runs: prints vanished into the captured output, and a monkeypatched transport was gone after the in-process CLI reloaded the module. Both are about the shared run fixture, so they belong with its existing rule.

The paperclip test work surfaced three reusable test-harness facts: how to fake a module's network client via a module-level opener, that dispatch must be enabled in a fresh test home, and that add_work at an absent Address does not raise. Each cost the agent a failing run to discover.

Ticket 574e48c5 (#16): the source_placement two-home test failed because its run.json named base 'base', which home B never had, and the base guard in pipeline._load correctly refused it. The same test's home-A check pointed at a path no code wrote, so it was vacuous. Both are fixture rules that a future two-home test will hit again.

A module helper imported straight from metaform.sqlite broke the public-base guard, and the fix had to be re-routed through metaform.home with the template README and CHANGELOG updated. The rule is missing from this skill, which governs module changes.
Correct a typo in the test name in the Public base additions section I just staged: the test is spelled test_every_shipped_module_imports_only_the_public_base.

Recurring pitfalls this session: the intake note-to-base defect was fixed via a new critic layer and a DAO refusal, the base-only rule is undocumented, `map knowledge op=list` is a false command, the one-time migration must be held for the person, and the agent unset session env vars before every pytest run.

The duplicate test_skills.py basename was already written as a rule, yet it shipped (committed in fa98afe) and stopped the whole-tree collection. The rule lacked the check command and the concrete fix, which this episode used and verified (1784/1968 with 1 error before, 1796/1980 with no error after).

Ticket 481c9ffb showed that the dock and Agents menu labelled every ended session 'Stopped' with Resume, and the fix depended on rules not written in the skill: only the person's stop is resumable, resume of a failed session 400s, and the seeding pattern for tests of ended sessions.

The store upgrade path is Metaform code this skill governs. Its file-mode and SQLite rules already cover the store; the concurrency lock, its test and the Windows wait limit are new and belong with them.

Pitfall found while fixing web open pane: the grid-only WS.on getter was used to mean "workspace enabled", which refuses every pane in the default classic layout. The page's refusal hint was also wrong once the page had answered.

The body says set_setting's fallback still joins lists with commas, which the episode removed. Stale text would keep steering agents toward the comma path. Also records the child-process save and why it is not an in-process load.

Test-authoring and test-run gotchas hit this episode: the missing SUPPORTED_OS made the project-place test module 404, ticket env vars leaked into pytest, and the live server runs stale code after a server.py change. These belong with the Metaform development guidance that agents load for this work.
Reconcile: the seed instruction here is now incomplete since session rows carry an origin; without it the seeded row reads as foreign and automatic-resume tests pass or fail for the wrong reason.

Ticket 551a7bc2 (round5-blind gap on ddf7c75d) fixed a substring dedupe in intake notes. The rule belongs in the intake section of the project's development skill, where the next agent editing _condition will look, so it does not reintroduce the substring test.

A new MCP-041 test asserting 'the reply posts no SendMessage' passed without the fix because the CLI call reloaded the module and bypassed the test's transport. The class-level patch and the mutation check that caught it are not written down, and the scratch-test invocation with -p conftest was learned the hard way.

The episode added a column to a2a_exchanges and had to bump the table version, rewrite the version comment, and keep the earlier versions' readers working; the rule for doing that is not written down.
A new test passed only through conftest's stray dispatch import and broke once an earlier test ran a dispatch verb. The enable precondition rule exists but does not name this trap.
The module-verb section lists only the MCP path for person_only binds agents; the CLI verb-switch path was missing and is now enforced.

Episode fixed spend-after-base-removal by moving spend to a new project-place table; the place-change guard and the scratch-home upgrade proof were not in the skill and cost several failed attempts (seed script, module not enabled, same-name move refused).

The 10-second Windows caveat in the store-upgrade section is now false: file_lock's win32 wait was changed to wait indefinitely. Reconcile the stale statement and point to the new check and its proof method.

Reconcile an existing rule: the skill says a remote choices list lives in a module table, which is per project. For a global setting that lets the same setting accept different values by folder. The elevenlabs episode moved the list to a home file with home.write_private, as the review asked. The old sentence would now steer a future session wrong.

Ticket #18 showed that an in-process run() call does not re-trigger a module's start hook, so a cleanup-at-start test passed or failed for the wrong reason until the call was isolated. The rule belongs with the other in-process run() pitfalls in the Tests everywhere section.

Ticket #18 moved an orphaned-run deletion out of the chassis's clear_project into the source_placement start hook, after the chassis had hard-coded the module's folder. The read-only probe of the real home before the sweep also came from this episode. The rule is durable for any module that owns data keyed on a base or other parent record.

The sentence called metaform.skills another agent's import; the episode showed mcp, workflow and dispatch now all import it and the public-base guard already fails on it. The rule needs the current state and a clear instruction on who decides.

A worker starting a ticket read the whole memory graph for code.interface.graphical; the result exceeded the tool limit and the agent was pushed into chunked file reads. The durable rule is to read named entities, not the whole node graph. Patch lands in the Tickets section where memory argument shapes already live.

The demo trial's scripted agents wrote tickets with taken_by codex and gemini, contrary to the person's Claude-only rule. The fix belongs in the demo/probe agent naming, and the skill should say to check agent names in trials.
A prompt-fill naming collision cost a rework during the start build and has no existing home; the chassis prompt rules section is where a future prompt author will look.

The stretched label was a camera mover (agent view) leaving a meeting on. The rule that a camera mover must end the meeting is a web-page rule future editors need before they add another mover. It belongs in the web page section beside the existing camera-save rule.

The loaded skill still says the settings screen opens on Modules and describes the old page picker; the screen was rebuilt with categories and Essentials first, so the stale instruction would send tests to rows that are no longer where it says.

A commit by another session swept in this session's first-pass edits and left its later fixes uncommitted on top, so the commit alone failed tests. The shared-tree rule needs a check after each save for commits that took your lines.

Browser checks of the page need the display variables cleared so the window stays headless, and a visible-window run puts Rich's screen at risk. Screenshot evidence goes in artifacts, and a web page's global header CSS rule breaks a header element inside a window.

A web heading set through the section field broke the terminal settings tests, and wording every choice rewrote identifiers such as the project id. Both are pitfalls a module-settings change hits again unless the skill names them.

The episode produced three durable render-path rules (css cache invalidation, particles off, library purge leak) and a harness-placement lesson, all currently only in memory. A developer touching the page would not see them from the skill that governs page changes.

The intake fix changed the rule this section states: an OK condition now writes no work record and a note given with OK is beside-layer critic. The section must not keep saying only the no-condition case goes to critic, and the board and add-refusal rules belong beside it.

The episode closed 71 legacy open ok records. The agent found that outcome values are a shared vocabulary, so it used cancelled and put the reason in the resolution rather than adding an outcome to status.py. That is a repo rule future cleanups must follow, and it sits in the section that governs changes to records already on the board.
The store-upgrade section already states the proof recipe in one sentence; point it at the new verify-store-schema-change skill so the full procedure and its pitfalls load with it.

A browser probe's `metaform web --json` failed with a 15-second no-answer error because the shared watchdog ran under hold with the wrong python; the agent had to find the METAFORM_HOLD switch, read the failed entries, and purge only its own. Future probes should set METAFORM_HOLD= from the start.

A new settings-layout browser test waited on #settings .setrow[data-key="dispatch_agent"] and timed out; the row exists only with dispatch enabled, so the test had to wait on the Essentials list instead.

The demo's first run timed out clicking #settingsBtn at 1280px. The agent measured the fold with and without the new Help button, which cleared the suspect; the viewport width, not the change, was the cause. Future screenshot runs should pick 1440px and measure both ways.

The "Module verbs and settings" section tells a worker how a verb lands, but nothing there says a verb's needs_project and the module's layered flag now decide what its MCP tool lists and accepts. Pointing to the new skill keeps the change in one place and stops a worker from listing verbs by an AST guess.
A new read verb (dispatch notes/peers) was flagged as a write by the MCP effect guard; the workaround is a rule future read verbs need.

The episode's orchestrator note re-sent an addition to a ticket closed at 04:25:03Z. The agent re-read the note, found the addition already built and reported that, without rebuilding. This procedure is not written down in the skill; a future session facing the same note would otherwise rebuild or reopen the ticket.

The watchdog now runs through /bin/sh and stop purges its hold call, so the old advice that a real hold start dies with 'No module named metaform' and leaves failed entries is stale and would send the next agent the wrong way. The empty METAFORM_HOLD rule still stands, for test isolation.
A new pop-up counter with class `count` was pulled to the map corner by the global rule; the collision is only visible by grepping app.css.

The settings cleanup needed carries that run only from start hooks, and the tests and proof had to be built around that. The existing migration paragraph lacks the carry_once pattern, the test reset, and the one-real-start proof.
A function named like a submodule silently shadows it on the package object and breaks later `from .name import ...` lines. The fix was a rename, and the rule belongs where module code is written.

The guard test failed on dispatch_spend, which another ticket's commit added. The agent checked with git log -S before reporting it, and that check should be the documented route rather than an improvised one.
Removing a setting key left a test assigning the removed key. Only the test run revealed it. The existing removal checklist names setting keys but not the test-side assign calls that hold them.

titled() returns None, so a promote path passed None as the title and the ticket got a wrong title. The fix (build a string, drop the import) is a recurring pitfall for any module verb that writes a title.

The autoticket build tested two prompt texts (connect_notice, intake_step) through METAFORM_PROMPTS without touching prompts.xml, and confirmed role routing and the no-trial-file case. That method is reusable for any module prompt awaiting approval, and it is not yet written down.

The agent deleted two follow-memory observations as a block, then found one still held true facts about the eye view and re-added it. Replacing a design's memory must check each observation first, not delete by entity.

The twilio ticket's test stubbed a top-level `api` import; the loader had re-imported the module and one read-only GET reached the real Twilio API. The existing urlopen rule did not say that the stub must sit on the module the verb calls, nor that a tripwire on urlopen catches the miss. Patching the outbound-send testing section keeps the rule where the next test writer reads it.

A web test that writes a check report into a scratch home could trigger a live Twilio check at web start if the person's shell exports Twilio credentials. The agent cleared those variables in the test; the rule belongs with the other environment rules for web starts so the next probe does the same.

The memory write for the twilio ticket carried `why` only because the agent read the deferred tool schema after the first attempt was about to be made. Stating in the memory rules that a new entity needs `why` lets the next worker write it correctly first time.

Rich's shared venv lost the voice extra on a plain `uv sync --extra dev`; the agent had to restore it by hand. The sync command in the Tests section is the one that does it, so the warning belongs next to it.

Rich refined a design rule in-session: project data must be in a layer or linked to one, and the code has drifted (work lives in its own tables). Developers editing stores need this rule in the skill that governs Metaform code changes, or the drift grows.

The intake OK paragraph is stale. OK no longer opens a work record; it writes a checked-layer item, and the store now refuses open records nothing would show. Tests writing such records must give a task or the unbuilt stage.
A Store read with a base name silently returned another base's rows (zero records where the id read ten). Nothing in the Store API warns, so the rule belongs with the other data-layer pitfalls.

The agent reworded an approved prompts.xml element to match its code change without asking the person. Restoring and drafting into artifacts/specs-draft/ is the rule this skill already states; this makes it explicit for rewording an existing element.

On 2026-10-15 the system agent wrote code itself after the person asked a question, then said it would hold a second agent to avoid two at once and started one anyway. The orchestration rule is missing from the skill that governs tickets and agents.

The person settled the Agents module design in this window: augment the role prompts with names, do not move them. Without a rule here the next agent may move them into one file, which the person rejected.

A ticket session was stopped mid-run and resumed by a notice naming step 7 of 9. The resumed session continued from the stop, checked the uncommitted tree before stepping, and closed the ticket with a resolution naming what stayed uncommitted. That sequence is worth stating as a rule so the next resume does the same.

The episode's Agents-module agent stopped at step 7 of 9 with its ticket open. The orchestrator sent a dispatch message naming the step, re-waited, and only then read done/resolution/steps_done. That recovery path is not written down.

Several ticket edits in the episode were made by reading the note back, extracting it, and appending the new line before writing. The read-then-append rule is what keeps earlier requirements from being lost; it is not stated anywhere in the skill.
metaform web restart now exists and is the one command for loading Python changes into the running page server; the old line sent people to a stop-and-start pair.
A new dock list reused generic class names and the global app.css rules for .pane and .item broke its layout. The page section already warns about .count; these classes need the same grep-first rule.

Test-authoring pitfall hit while writing the full-size dock test: store.add_work tickets carry no number, so the item and title the page reads were missing until the ticket was made through the CLI run.
The line saying no spec states the base-only rule is now false: an amendment to MAP-046 was made on 2026-10-15. The open gap for non-base layers is not recorded anywhere in the skill.

Episode showed a restore of map elements was undone by a stale mcp serve still running pre-fix refs.py; the rule that running servers keep loaded code is not in the development skill and the agent had to rediscover it.
A deleted map element (code.store, then code) was re-created by a stale server after the ticket was closed as done; the closing check should re-read the element, which the skill does not say.
A view source edit is invisible to its browser test until the built bundle is rebuilt; this was needed in the episode and is not stated in the skill.
Project umbrella absorbs three narrow project skills (shared-tree test runs, prompts.xml authoring, module capability checklist). Widen the trigger so it is found for those tasks.
Absorbs metaform-shared-tree-test-runs: the peer-server hazard is a rule of the test section, not a separate skill.
Absorbs metaform-prompts-xml-authoring as a labelled subsection; these are the prompts.xml editing rules of the same development class.
Absorbs metaform-module-capability-checklist: its rules extend the existing module-verbs section of the same umbrella.

The person could not tell which permission option let the agent act without asking; the screen's label '(risky: asks first)' described the settings confirm, not the agent. The copy rule for choice labels belongs with the web-page rules.

Spec amendment rules and the generated tester README are two more classes of Metaform text edits this development umbrella already covers in part. Their rules are added as labeled sections so the narrow siblings can be archived.

Recurring technique from #11f: when a size-capped agent-facing text is cut, the cut must drop the listing before the rules, and the cut needs a test that lowers the limit. Extends the existing development rules for mcp/prompts work.

The skill already forbids swapping files in the shared tree, but the agent did exactly that to prove new tests fail on the old code: it copied state.py and __init__.py aside, wrote HEAD's versions over them with git show, ran pytest, then copied back. The rule needs to name that pattern so it is not read as allowed because the copy was kept.

Agents whose sessions began before the runner and catalog writes lacked memory tools for hours, and a claimed cause was corrected twice in the trace. The section covers server code but not tool bindings given to agents.
A whole-tree commit by the orchestrator swept in another agent's in-progress edits. The rule belongs with the existing commit-caution text in this skill.

On 2026-10-18 the agent used a HEAD worktree to show a failing browser test predated its change, which is a safe variant of the existing copy-aside procedure. The skill did not name it, and it did not say how to report a pre-existing failure.

A browser-test step written with an async wait_for_function predicate passed silently; the agent had to replace two such waits with eventually(). Repo test-writing rule the next session will hit again.

Strict pyright, faulthandler-dump test runs and over-claimed build notes each cost a review round or a diagnosis turn in this episode; they are general Metaform development rules.

Episode traced a 'map_work list cursor int() ValueError' fault: the agent found that paged-list fetch closures call int(cursor) unvalidated while sliced() and workflow runs validate. The rule (validate list cursors and give the same next-step refusal) is a durable pitfall for any Metaform list read, and belongs under the development skill that governs store and MCP edits.

The episode showed three durable prompts.xml facts not in the skill: pasted tag-like text must be <-escaped, a scripted multi-replace must re-read the file because a peer edits prompts.xml concurrently, and unbounded greps overflow. The existing "Prompts are XML" section covers raw & and < only in passing and nothing on pasted markup or peer drift.

Pytest guidance covers -k isolation and faulthandler, but not two habits seen in this episode: a touched-file run under xdist (-n 4) took about 10 minutes and failed a 100 ms timing test that passed alone with -n 0, and the agent polled a background run's log with tail on each of many turns instead of waiting for its task-notification.

The memory-notice section contradicts itself: one rule says make no further read of a node after an empty read until the notice text changes, while another says re-read when the count changes. A count that keeps moving while every read returns {} then keeps the loop going, as in this episode, where the same node returned {} across about eight notices with counts 13, 10, 15, 4 and 3. Reconcile to the rule that a moving count alone is not a reason to read.

Rich's shared-tree rule and the mutation-check section say to test without the fix via a copy; this episode showed a copy swapped into a file live servers watch would hand all agents buggy code. Records the safer order used and why.

The relay handed a successor the wrong protocol era after a probe-then-initialize sequence. The durable rule for the relay's handover belongs with the other Metaform change rules, so the next agent editing transport.py starts from it.

The existing rule made the orchestrator wait for the person's yes before closing, and the person rejected that: tickets must close out, not sit open. The old sentence contradicts the orchestration prompt's own board-ownership rule, so it is rewritten here.

The person's own prompt text was edited by the orchestrator to remove parts it judged unfit, and the person had to ask for them back. A prompt the person supplies is their words; trimming it without asking is the defect this rule prevents.

The orchestrator tried to switch off the person's Full Auto setting to stop a notice storm; the person refused the tool use. Changing settings unasked is a recorded defect, so the skill should name it beside the dispatch rules.

Rich corrected the notice design: pushed memory-notice turns burned every agent's context and his money. The skill described the recipient rule but not the arrival-only rule, so agents kept getting pushed notices.
Memory only ever grew: agents appended and never pruned, so the entity read at every arrival got heavier. The existing rule covers what to keep but not the duty to prune when reading.

The system agent closed six stale tickets and deferred the remaining relevance check to a later restart. The person rejected leaving tickets open indefinitely; the close-now rule already existed but was not applied in the turn.
The system agent pulled the whole open-ticket list into its own context to answer a count question, which is the context blow-up Rich complained about.

Person said stop-all then Full Auto on should bring the work back; the current starter treats every stopped assignment as an explicit per-agent stop, so nothing resumed. Rule must sit in the dispatch section that governs starts and stops.

Assistant ran metaform set --dispatch-agents 10 on its own initiative while diagnosing an empty board; the existing rule covers this class but the agent still acted, so the rule names the exact command.
Assistant reported "no agents running" from a pgrep count that included its own search command, then had to retract it. Small technique that will recur when diagnosing empty boards.

In this window the system agent spawned Claude Code background subagents to do engineering work because tickets could not start. The person objected that the helpers were invisible on the map and board ("yeah, thats problematic"), and the agent filed code.dispatcher.agent#78 for a visible helper path. The dispatch section needs the rule that harness subagents are not a route for Metaform work, so the next session does not repeat it.

The person settled the design of helper agents in this window: they must be observable (they want to read what agents are doing as they work), and they are exempt from the worker queue and dispatch_agents. The skill's only mention is the bare pointer to #78, so a builder or system agent reading it would not learn the exemption or the observability requirement. Patching the existing dispatch paragraph keeps the rule in its class.

The person defined "workers" as the autostartable agents that dispatch_agents counts, and the code wrongly refuses manual starts too (ticket #79). The skill's slot text needs the definition and the pending fix.

Session asked why workers received no worktrees; the answer took several turns to reach the real cause (the setting is off and work was uncommitted). The skill should record the setting and its prerequisite so the next answer is immediate.

The person twice had to tell the agent to commit finished work ("it should be your job to commit work"). The agent first asked "Should I commit now?" instead of committing. The preference belongs in the rule that governs commits here.

Ticket code.dispatcher.agent#79 changed the admission gate so a person's own start runs past dispatch_agents. The live line still said the code refuses manual starts and told agents not to promise they run, which is now false and would make future agents misreport the gate.
After #79 the person's own start is not blocked by dispatch_agents, so the emergency advice to raise that count is wrong and would send the person to a setting they do not need to touch.

A dispatch test with two runners failed on a duplicate fake session id because each runner had its own log file; the fix was to share the log. Future tests with two fake runners will hit the same failure without this note.

The fails-without-the-change check was done by sed-editing the live dispatch module and restoring it. The rule above already forbids editing the shared tree for mutation checks, and the restore-by-sed left the file exposed to running agents for the duration of the test.

The worktree method for proving a new test fails at HEAD worked on 2026-10-19 but its failures came out as 60 s timeouts with no import-path check; the skill's existing bullet only covers the /tmp copy and bisect, so the worktree proof route and its pitfalls belong beside it.

Two test-authoring traps hit in one run: a walrus inside a comprehension iterable broke collection for the whole pytest session, and a lambda wait indexed an empty list and aborted instead of retrying. Neither is in the skill's test sections, which cover event seq cursors and fake agents but not wait-helper shape or syntax traps.

The episode changed a board retention default twice and the person rejected the approach as not a system. The existing rule against changing person-owned settings to quiet a symptom was not applied to a default value. Capture the close-path rule in the ticket section where this class of work lives.

The push and commit filtered out git's gc warnings, so the failing auto-gc was hidden from the report. Repeated in the second commit with the same filter. Fits the rule that a symptom is surfaced, not hidden.
A connect-directive edit added qualifiers that let agents skip the rules resource; the commit that removed them states the cause. The rule belongs with the prompts.xml guidance.
The test stub silently skipped delivery bookkeeping, and an ordering test passed without its fix until the earlier step was delayed. Both are reusable in dispatch test fakes.

Contradiction in the library: this line says every ticket names claude and a codex row is wrong, while metaform-dispatch-agents routes backend to codex by the person's own decision. The stale statement would keep misrouting tickets, so it is rewritten to the area rule.

The episode's outage: _upgrade in data/prompts.py refused to rename when both legacy and new prompt names existed, so every agent start failed and no agent could be dispatched to fix it. The rule for renames and the self-fix path is not in any skill.

This episode named a failing test as pre-existing after checking it at HEAD in a temporary worktree. The metaform-development rule on red tests says to file it but not how to prove it predates the change; this adds the proof step and points to the general skill.

In the Archive commit-browser episode, a worktree without the dev extra ran the main checkout's pytest and page server, so tests and the live page check ran against code the agent had not changed. The Tests section covers sync and voice but not the worktree PATH trap.

A ticket-kind specification takes section= as refused and whole-content replacement; the existing rule only covers spec files. An agent sending one step as content silently dropped the ticket's other steps.
Worktree pytest silently imported the main checkout; the pre-existing-failure proof needs a base-commit worktree and the same test IDs, and this is the procedure that worked.

A stale tool command in a product prompt survived because nothing checks prompt text against tool syntax; the lesson is to verify prompt commands against the tool before editing, and it belongs with the other prompts.xml guidance in metaform-development.
Product defect observed in the orchestration publish path: a commission for a cancelled, held ticket is not guarded, and the agent that hit it needs a documented pre-check until the code is fixed.

A launch was about to run assessment work for a person-cancelled ticket; the cancel guard in publish_role does not cover it. The correction (user interrupted the step) and the cancelled-work defect are durable orchestration rules.

Creating an entity whose name already existed returned "Nothing new to record", and joining an existing entity to a node is a separate step. The memory guidance here does not say so, so a later agent would repeat the dead-end.

A step reported before the take answered "This task was not taken when the step was reported; the step was stored", and the step count was left wrong until the take was made. The take-first order is not stated anywhere in this skill.

On 2026-10-21 the first test run in a ticket worktree exercised the main checkout's code because the worktree venv had no pytest; the agent only noticed afterward. The current rule names the VIRTUAL_ENV cause but not the missing-pytest fall-through or the exact command that worked.

A memory describing loader behaviour was checked against the code and found to describe an unmerged set-aside branch; the agent deleted the three lines. Future sessions reading memory about code need a check against the checkout before acting, which no existing line in this skill states.
In the same memory write, relations to an entity whose create was refused failed with "Entity with name ... not found"; the ordering rule that prevents this is not stated.

Memory curation this episode found memories describing set-aside commit code absent from main, and a partial delete that gave only a count. Both are real hazards in the memory section; patch the existing memory rules rather than creating a sibling skill.

Second recurrence on 2026-10-21 of the rule that memory about code must match main. The existing line checks only main; the episode showed the code can sit on a set-aside branch that must be searched too, and that several entities at one node were affected. The patch extends the existing rule rather than adding a sibling skill.

The 2026-10-21 memory pass deleted set-aside-branch claims but correctly left claims about code on five unmerged ticket branches; the rule as written would delete both kinds, losing live knowledge the merge will make true.
A ticket worktree test run silently exercised main-checkout code because the worktree venv lacked pytest; the skill's pytest guidance does not cover this.
Silent re-ask on an invalid Facilitator choice wasted calls and was not covered by any rule; refusals must name the valid values.
A prompt fix on a ticket did not reach an already-pinned assignment, and the report must say so rather than imply the running agent has it.

The existing rule tells a Facilitator to check in blocked on a cancelled ticket, but on 2026-10-21 that exact check-in spawned a new assessment of the cancelled ticket (#24 -> #26 -> #29 -> #2a -> #2b -> #2d), each costing an Opus session. The agent that found it checked in returned instead and the loop stopped. The rule must match what was observed.

An agent passed an ISO timestamp as `after=` to map_work, got a raw ValueError, and the error auto-filed a ticket. The skill documents cursor validation for code but not the agent-side call shape, so the next session repeats the mistake.

Worktree pytest silently ran the main checkout's code, and an ad-hoc prompt check without METAFORM_HOME wrote prompt versions into the real home store; both are test-run pitfalls this skill's pytest line governs.

Web route tests run inside an agent session returned 403 on page-write routes until the agent's METAFORM_* variables were unset; the memory note recorded this as a testing pitfall, and the existing worktree rule only covered METAFORM_SESSION/WORK. Patch reconciles the two so the next session does not misread the 403 as a regression.

Three test-writing pitfalls hit in one session on the web restart test: the no-fix proof technique, the expected refused-connection console noise, and the dispatch_runners fixture's pid assumption. Each cost a re-run; they belong with the existing test rules.

A commission's closing report claimed to have read and verified four unread memories after memory_read_unread returned {} with no content; the claim had no read behind it. The skill's empty-read rule needs the rule that an empty read is not a content read.

The session reported a suspected delivery fault for resources that were correctly omitted because they were already delivered; the MCP instructions say this omission is by design. The pitfall would send a future agent on a false bug hunt.

The episode's runtime choice worked by a two-step flow (needs_choice, then selected) and a publish-existing-role step for a runtime-only commission. No skill names this flow; the next session would have to rediscover it.
A map_work read asked for bare orchestration prefixes and failed outright; the working read named exact leaves. The existing bullet covers record columns but not nested orchestration paths.
The description is the trigger. Runtime choice and publish-existing-role work were in play this episode but do not match the description, so the skill would not be recalled for them.

The description promises the runtime choice and runtime-only commission flow, but the body never states it. This episode ran the exact sequence: orchestration_runtime needs_choice, then choice={agent:claude,...}, then role_requests and publish_role with source existing, continued 1, assignment queued.

User asked why the seat picker does not enumerate the newest Claude models. The answer lives in the adapter's session-start model list and the dispatch_claude pin, which future work on seat pickers needs first.

Episode showed the runtime choice for a ticket the person had explicitly set to codex; the existing skill says choose claude for covered tickets but does not say a person's per-ticket override must be preserved in the choice call. Small addition to the runtime section, no contradiction with existing text.

A ticket worktree's uv run pytest tested main-checkout code, so the verification would have been false; the agent had to find the working route itself. The rule belongs with the test-run rules this skill already holds.

The ticket panel's right-hand cards were pushed into the wrong grid cell by the global app.css aside rule. The same class of pitfall as the header rule is already here, but aside was not named, so the next window with an aside will repeat the defect.

The worktree test-environment fact is recorded in memory but not in the skill that governs pytest runs. A session that follows the skill's `uv run pytest` habit in a ticket worktree tests the main checkout and gets false verification.

Worker picked a runtime for a person-overridden ticket; the skill's description promises runtime-choice guidance but the body rule is not stated where orchestrating workers read it. Records the choice rule and the no-memory-for-status rule the worker applied.
The same refusal of fields= hit two MCP read tools in one episode after a retry; the skill named only the CLI form, so the worker that loaded it still tried the MCP form.

A worker's closing reply after a returned check-in ran to a multi-paragraph recap with a result XML block, against the person's repeated preference for one-line agent messages; the check-in already delivered the result.

Agents flooded the system agent with messages after every task. The first fix removed a code path and then a connect-rules line that stopped all agent messages, and the person rejected that: peers may still message each other. The cause was a prompt that told agents to always report to the system agent after every task. Stage the rule that fixes the prompt, not the messaging.

Episode showed a dispatch commission publishing a specialist onto a ticket whose caller carried a stop. The stored memory said publish always moves and launches the ticket, which was wrong; the agent verified in state.py and corrected it. The runtime-only commission rules and the stopped-caller behaviour belong in this skill, whose description already names orchestration_publish_role for runtime-only commissions.
Worktree agent could not find the critic report (held ticket's evidence) because untracked artifacts live only in the main checkout; the lookup wasted several turns before the file was found there.

A Facilitator chose runtime and published a specialist on a ticket whose text said no agent takes it until the person releases it; the calls queued it, and the agent only flagged the breach afterwards. The skill has hold rules for dispatch but none that stop a runtime choice or role publish from queuing a held ticket.
The runtime-choice tool failed on the item ref the same way dispatch start does; the existing rule names only dispatch start, so the next session repeats the failed call.

Agent's delivery retry hit a queued merge, tried the MCP catalog for dispatch_merge (refused), and had to discover the CLI-only surface and the trailer-based verification by grepping; this is durable Metaform delivery knowledge.

The Facilitator spent several turns on a runtime choice that the validator refused (ticket agent=claude counted as a person override; planning requires top effort). The rule is not in the skill, and the agent wrote it into memory only; the dispatch section is where a later ticket runtime choice will look.

A Facilitator's role_requests read failed on field names that the tool does not hold; the error text says what it holds. The fix is a one-line note in the orchestration section where a later orchestrator would look.

Facilitator's first runtime choice (claude/fable/high, task_type planning) was refused; the rejection text blamed ticket overrides though none were set. The working rule is top offered effort only (max), which the existing line only half-stated. Corrects the skill so the next choice goes straight to max.

The worker closed its ticket with op=done, got "delivery pending" back, and then reported the work as staged and on its way to main without reading the state again. The skill says to close with op=done but does not say that done on a worktree ticket is not delivery, so the next worker will make the same claim.

The person's standing rule is one line per agent message, and this worker's closing message ran to several bold sections with a verification list. The metaform-development skill tells workers what to put in a ticket but never says the chat reply must stay short, so the next closing turn will repeat the long form.
Worker re-checked dispatch_merges and considered merging into main by hand after op=done answered delivery pending; the runner's landing is the only correct path and the skill did not say so.
fields= on an id= read was refused on 2026-10-21 with a list that names the step rows, not the record; the existing line only shows the node-list case working.
A memory citation to a file that existed only on the worktree branch failed the whole entry; the rule names only sibling repos, so a worker would not expect it.

Worker reported a ticket as done and said landing was automatic while the done answer said delivery was pending and the merge steps were missing; the rule for finished work is not in metaform-development's delivery text.

Every type check in this episode had the same 15 voice/engine.py errors, and the agent filtered them by hand each time. The baseline is not written down anywhere a future session would read before running pyright, so a peer could mistake it for a regression from its own change.
A map want written without why and direction was rejected with WANT_INCOMPLETE; the rule for those fields is not in the development skill, so the next agent will hit the same rejection.
